text:
driftbot: Preflight simulation finished for PR #4827 (deploy/gpu-pool).
Summary: projected eu-west-1 GPU capacity shortfall of ~2 nodes during 08:00-10:00 UTC peak. Helm diff highlights label/taint mismatch on nodepool (gpu: true vs gpu: present). OPA policy 'no-spot-gpu' flagged 1 resource.

maya: pinging @arjun @lina — driftbot suggests autoscaler bump or add reserved nodes. link: https://ci.redwood.local/preflight/4827 :eyes:

arjun: can you paste the helm --dry-run output? I want to see the exact taint change.

maya: sure — ran locally:
```bash
helm upgrade --install gpu-pool ./charts/gpu-pool \ 
  --namespace infra --values values-prod.yaml --set autoscaler.maxNodes=40 --dry-run
```
output snippet:
```yaml
nodePool:
  labels:
    gpu: "true"
  taints:
    - key: "dedicated"
      value: "gpu"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
```
staging currently has `gpu: present` label and no taint. Helm diff shows kubelet automount mismatch for pods that rely on taint-based scheduling.

lina: risk: if we change labels/taints without a rollout plan, some older DaemonSets that pin to label `gpu: present` will not land and jobs will queue. Customer-facing latency spike possible. Cost tradeoff: 2 reserved v100 nodes ~ $4k/mo; spot fallback risk increases.

arjun: what's blocking auto-apply in CI? Is it the OPA policy failure or quota in eu-west-1?

driftbot: OPA denies: `deny["no-spot-gpu"]` because chart sets `spot: true` in values-prod.yaml. GitOps preflight also reported quota_alert: `gpu.quota==95%` for eu-west-1 (forecasted peak). Both must be resolved before auto-merge.

maya: options:
- update values to `spot: false` and bump reserved capacity (fast, more cost)
- add a canary nodepool with different labels to avoid label swap (safer)
- update OPA allowlist for this PR (needs approvals)

lina: prefer canary nodepool. We can create a small reserved pool (2 nodes) with explicit labels, point a subset of jobs to it via nodeSelector, then live-validate.

arjun: agree. plan:
1) create canary nodepool in eu-west-1 (reserved, 2 nodes) with labels gpu:true and taint dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule
2) deploy helm chart with an overlay that maps critical jobs to the canary nodeSelector
3) run smoke tests for 45m
4) if good, scale up autoscaler to cover remainder and roll out full change

maya: I'll trigger a simulated deployment first (helm values overlay) and run the CI smoke in the canary namespace.

ops-bot: ticket INF-827 created: "eu-west-1 canary nodepool + preflight smoke" — assignee: maya, due: 2024-06-18

maya: kicking off canary create via terraform plan -> apply (dry-run showed no quota hard-fail, only soft-alert). Command:
```bash
terraform apply -var="region=eu-west-1" -target=module.gpu_canary_pool -auto-approve
```

deploy-bot: canary provision job started (job id c-9932). Estimated ready in 7m. I'll post status updates here.

arjun: thanks. reminder to add a quick health dashboard check: queued_job_depth, avg_inference_latency, eviction_count. If queued_job_depth > 5% baseline for 15m -> rollback.

lina: +1. Also capture cost delta in the alert so finance can triage if it becomes long-lived.

maya: will monitor. if OPA still blocks after canary, we'll open an ops-exemption and cut a short-lived policy update.

deploy-bot: canary provision complete — nodes ready.

driftbot: smoke-run results: critical workloads scheduled on canary, no evictions, latency stable (+0.3% baseline), queued depth unchanged. OPA check OK (canary pool uses reserved, spot=false).

maya: looks green. proceeding to scale autoscaler by +2 and patch helm to migrate workloads to new label mapping in a canary rollout.

arjun: great — keep rollout slow. no mass label swaps. :thumbsup:

lina: filing post-mortem template in case drift recurs. tagging infra-runbooks.

ops-bot: INF-827 updated: canary succeeded -> next step scheduled (step 2: gradual autoscaler increase) in 30m.

maya: thanks team. will post a short status update to #all-hands once full rollout completes.
